capabilities.text: Use two to eight track points, evenly spaced from left to right
Set each point’s height, 0 to 100
Write a point’s label, like A, PE_g or KE = 0
capabilities.note: Letters A, B, C… are the opening state.

capabilities.text: Put a blank line in place of a point’s label
Leave a point unlabeled, so it only shapes the track
Write a point’s height mark, like 40 m, h or h/2
capabilities.note: The value with its unit is the opening state.

capabilities.text: Put a blank line in place of a height mark
Leave a height mark off
Put a loop at one point
Set the loop’s radius, in the heights’ units
capabilities.note: Token passes on the loop alone; checked by hand that the radius changes the loop render.

capabilities.text: Label the loop’s radius
capabilities.note: Token passes on the loop alone; checked by hand.

capabilities.text: Label the top of the loop
capabilities.note: Token passes on the loop alone; checked by hand.

capabilities.text: Ride a cart, a ball or a block
Label the object
Set the object’s size
Put the object at any point
Put the object upside down at the top of the loop
capabilities.note: Token passes on the loop alone; checked by hand.

capabilities.text: Draw the velocity forward or back along the track
capabilities.note: Ours draws it solid, not dashed (visual look).

capabilities.text: Make the stretch from any point to the next rough, hatched
Label a rough stretch with its friction
capabilities.note: Ours has a length mark for a rough stretch but no friction label.

capabilities.text: Mark a rough stretch’s length, like d or 12 m
capabilities.note: Token passes on the rough stretch alone; checked by hand.

capabilities.text: Turn the ground line on or off
Mirror the track to run right to left
Color the figure for slides
